title: api: schema versioning + deprecations, beta headers, backward-compat shims for OpenAI-compat
author: Ava Chen
description:
Motivation: as we continue to expand streaming features, tool/function calling, and structured output, downstream users (and our OpenAI-compat layer) have requested a clearer, opt-in mechanism for API schema changes and deprecations. This PR introduces a lightweight versioning model: Accept-Version and X-Redwood-Beta headers (server-side) plus runtime compatibility shims to preserve legacy behavior when requested. The goals are: 1) allow us to evolve request/response schemas safely, 2) provide clear deprecation/errors for clients on newer schemas, 3) keep streaming stability and function-calling behavior stable for existing consumers via opt-in/backcompat modes.

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds Accept-Version and X-Redwood-Beta header parsing in the API gateway and surfaces chosen schema version to downstream handlers.
- Implements a compatibility shim layer in redwood-openai-compat that can downgrade new response envelopes (structured outputs / tool-calls) to legacy OpenAI-like frames when clients request v1 or set the legacy-beta header.
- Adds deprecation metadata to model response schemas and emits structured deprecation warnings into response headers and telemetry when clients use deprecated fields.
- Stabilizes streaming framing: legacy chunked framing is preserved when legacy version is requested; new chunk framing (structured chunks with metadata) is default for v2+. Also fixes a regression where async tool call finish events could be emitted out-of-order under heavy batching.
- Adds E2E tests in eval-harness and unit tests in api/ to cover version negotiation, deprecation warnings, and streaming downgrade behavior.
- Updates OpenAPI and compatibility docs with migration steps and examples.

Rollout / migration plan:
- Feature gated behind runtime flag "api.schema_versioning" (default: enabled in main, can be disabled in Dedicated/Private for controlled rollout).
- Canary rollout to hosted infra for 24h with telemetry alerting on unexpected client errors (>0.1% increase in 4xx for API paths).
- Post-merge follow-ups: small analytics job to enumerate clients using v1 and send targeted notice emails; add SDK helpers in redwood-sdk-* to set Accept-Version easily.

Notes: this PR is intentionally conservative. It does not remove old fields; it adds shim/downgrade logic so we can ship server-side schema changes without immediate client breakage. Where behavior differs (streaming framing, tool-call result envelopes), we require explicit Accept-Version or X-Redwood-Beta: legacy header to receive legacy behavior.
commits: feat(api): add header parsing for Accept-Version and X-Redwood-Beta
feat(openai-compat): implement v1->v2 downgrades and shim helpers
fix(streaming): preserve legacy chunk framing when legacy-version requested; fix ordering regression for tool finish events
chore(tests): add E2E tests for schema negotiation and streaming downgrade
docs: compatibility guide and migration examples
review_comments: Diego Martinez: Great overall direction. Two asks: (1) can we expose structured telemetry for deprecated-field usage (not just log lines)? (2) add a health-check that asserts streaming ordering under load in CI.
Ava Chen (author): Added telemetry metric redwood.deprecation.usage with tag 'field' and pushed a new CI job 'streaming-order-check' that runs the ordering workload in a containerized harness.
Priya Rao: The shim code looks reasonable but we should avoid double-serialize paths that could increase tail latency. Suggest microbenchmarks and guardrails.

Ava Chen (author): Added microbenchmarks to perf-canary and a quick path that bypasses shims when Accept-Version==latest; measured median add ~0.8ms in our canary GPU nodes. Included notes in comments and toggles via config.
Liam O'Connor: Please add a clear migration snippet to the SDK docs showing how to set Accept-Version and the consequence on streaming frames. Also mark X-Redwood-Beta as 'temporary' in docs.
Ava Chen (author): Documentation updated in docs/openapi/compatibility.md and SDK examples folder. Marked beta header and added warning line.
release_notes: Introduced API schema version negotiation (Accept-Version / X-Redwood-Beta), backward-compatibility shims for the OpenAI-compat layer, deprecation headers and telemetry for deprecated fields, and streaming framing stabilization. See docs/openapi/compatibility.md for migration steps and examples.
